active_recommendations.title: Suspicious IP-address links
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider configuring web gateways and email filters to flag links that use raw IP addresses where legitimate business traffic normally uses approved domain names.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Substantial proportion of phishing samples utilize raw IP addresses instead of domains.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Raw IP address links ('having_IP_Address == -1') observed in 1927 of 4899 cases (39.33%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: Describes historical phishing feature distributions in the stored dataset.
Does not claim that all IP-address URLs are malicious.
Does not inspect live organizational gateway configurations.

active_recommendations.title: Lookalike domain protection
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider deploying domain-impersonation checks that compare external domains with your organization's domains and trusted business partners.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Extremely prevalent hyphenated domain structure observed across phishing cases.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Prefix/suffix hyphenation ('Prefix_Suffix == -1') observed in 4898 of 4899 cases (99.98%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: The prefix/suffix feature indicates hyphenation syntax; it is not proof that a domain impersonates a specific brand.
Phrase findings as a signal worth reviewing rather than confirmed impersonation.

active_recommendations.title: Suspicious subdomain review
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider reviewing URL inspection policies for unusually nested subdomains and destinations designed to make untrusted websites appear legitimate.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: High prevalence of complex/multi-level subdomain nesting in phishing samples.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Suspicious subdomain nesting observed in 4089 of 4899 cases (83.47%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: Subdomain feature encoding reflects dot count in host portion.
Does not claim that the feature alone identifies malicious subdomains.

active_recommendations.title: HTTPS and certificate validation
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider ensuring that web security controls validate TLS certificates and the actual destination hostname, rather than treating the presence of HTTPS as proof that a website is trustworthy.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Untrusted or invalid TLS certificates are prominent in phishing data.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Untrusted TLS state ('SSLfinal_State == -1') observed in 3052 of 4899 cases (62.30%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: The HTTPS_token feature (URL token) and SSLfinal_State feature (certificate trust) are not interchangeable.
Does not infer real certificate validity from a URL string token alone.

active_recommendations.title: URL parsing and normalization
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider strengthening URL parsing and normalization in email and web filters so that unusually long or obfuscated links receive additional inspection.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: A heavy majority of phishing samples exhibit long, complex URL strings (>75 chars).
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Long URL indicator ('URL_Length == -1') observed in 4080 of 4899 cases (83.28%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: URL length categorization is based on static character count thresholds.
Does not label a URL as obfuscated solely because it is long.

active_recommendations.title: External link inspection
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider requiring security inspection of links in incoming emails before users visit external destinations, especially when the destination is unfamiliar.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: High prevalence of deceptive external link structural indicators.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Suspicious external link feature ('Prefix_Suffix == -1') observed in 4898 of 4899 cases (99.98%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: Does not claim that the database contains email messages or sender identities.
Reflects recurring external link structural features identified in historical phishing data.

active_recommendations.title: Domain reputation checks
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider integrating domain reputation and threat-intelligence checks into email and web gateways, with safeguards to minimize false positives.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Ubiquitous domain structure manipulation in phishing vectors.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Suspicious domain structure observed in 4898 of 4899 cases (99.98%), supporting deployment of reputation verification layers.
limitations: Based on observed recurring domain-level signals in historical phishing vectors.
Does not make external queries to third-party domain reputation APIs.

active_recommendations.title: Security awareness training
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider providing employees with practical training on recognizing deceptive links, checking destination domains, and reporting suspicious messages.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Extensive volume of historical phishing examples demonstrates need for continuous human sensor awareness.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Dataset comprises 4899 validated phishing vectors with 328 distinct archetypes, justifying continuous user education on deceptive links.
limitations: Dataset evidence demonstrates high diversity of deceptive link patterns.
Does not claim the dataset proves that employees have failed to recognize phishing.

active_recommendations.title: Lookalike-domain monitoring
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider monitoring for newly registered domains resembling your organization's brand and creating a process for triaging likely impersonation attempts.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Near-universal adoption of domain manipulation tactics in phishing population.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Domain manipulation signal ('Prefix_Suffix == -1') observed in 4898 of 4899 cases (99.98%), supporting brand impersonation monitoring.
limitations: Does not claim that the project has discovered newly registered domains or performed external domain monitoring.
Reflects measured prevalence of domain syntax patterns associated with impersonation.

active_recommendations.title: Safe URL detonation
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider opening suspicious links only in an isolated analysis environment with controlled network access, rather than on employee workstations.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Dominant threat clusters represent high-density risk patterns requiring contained handling.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Dominant threat archetype cluster 0 encompasses 2589 samples (52.85% of population).
limitations: The engine must not fetch, open, or detonate any URLs.
Reflects high concentrations of deceptive technical signals that warrant contained analysis.

active_recommendations.title: Web gateway policy review
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider reviewing secure web gateway policies to ensure suspicious destinations are inspected, blocked when justified, and logged for later investigation.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Multiple independent URL risk signals demonstrate pervasive circumvention tactics.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Identified 5 independently measured URL risk signals exceeding 20.0% prevalence in the phishing population.
limitations: Does not claim that an existing gateway is missing controls; the project does not inspect organizational infrastructure.

active_recommendations.title: Cluster-driven detection rules
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider reviewing the recurring feature combination and, if validated against real examples, creating a targeted detection rule in your existing email or web security controls.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Clustering identified robust, recurring archetypes representing large proportions of phishing cases.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Cluster 0 comprises 2589 records (52.85% of population), exceeding support thresholds.
limitations: Do not recommend a hard blocking rule solely because a cluster exists.
Clusters are descriptive groups, not proof of a specific coordinated campaign or attacker.

active_recommendations.title: Layered phishing defenses
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider using layered controls across email filtering, web reputation, domain validation, endpoint protection, and employee reporting rather than relying on a single detection signal.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Observed threat patterns simultaneously span multiple distinct security layers.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Observed robust threat signals across 2 distinct layers (domain_structure, network_transport), demonstrating need for defense-in-depth.
limitations: Do not count several correlated features as independent evidence without acknowledging their relationship.
Reflects diverse technical layers represented in observed threat patterns.

active_recommendations.title: Prioritize the strongest evidence
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider prioritizing a review of controls related to the most consistently observed phishing patterns, using the measured counts, prevalence, and validation status to guide effort.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Dominant signal observed with extreme prevalence across phishing population.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Rank 1 signal 'Prefix_Suffix == -1' observed in 4898 cases (99.98% of population), providing strong empirical grounding for focus.
limitations: Ranking is based on observed prevalence in historical phishing vectors.
Do not equate frequency with severity or assume the most frequent signal represents the highest business risk.

active_recommendations.title: Shortened URL protection
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider strengthening email and web security controls to expand shortened links safely, inspect their final destinations, and flag suspicious redirects.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Measured prevalence of shortened URLs in phishing dataset meets review threshold.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Shortened URL indicator ('Shortining_Service == -1') observed in 514 of 4899 phishing cases (10.49%), exceeding thresholds (50 count, 5.0%).
limitations: Describes historical phishing feature distributions in the stored dataset.
Does not assume every shortened URL is malicious.
Does not establish causation or confirm a particular attack campaign.

active_recommendations.title: Attachment and link defense
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider combining email link inspection with attachment scanning, sender authentication checks, and clear reporting procedures for suspicious messages.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: High variety and frequency of persistent link attack patterns.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Identified 12 distinct feature signals exceeding 25.0% support across 4899 phishing records.
limitations: This is a general defensive recommendation.
URL feature vectors do not establish that malicious attachments were present.

active_recommendations.title: Sender authentication
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider reviewing SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configurations for your organization's domains and monitoring failures that could indicate spoofing attempts.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Substantial domain and email-related threat indicators motivate authentication hardening.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Motivating signal 'Prefix_Suffix == -1' observed in 4898 of 4899 cases (99.98%), indicating widespread spoofing/impersonation tactics.
limitations: Dataset evidence motivates a control review rather than proving a sender-authentication failure.
The engine does not inspect an organization's SPF, DKIM, or DMARC records.

active_recommendations.title: Outbound web access controls
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider reviewing outbound web access policies, allowing only business-required services and ports, and logging policy violations for investigation.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Non-standard or restricted port usage detected in significant phishing cohort.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Non-preferred port indicator ('port == -1') observed in 735 of 4899 cases (15.00%), exceeding thresholds.
limitations: Port feature reflects non-preferred port usage in historical data.
Does not infer an actual destination port or a confirmed network-policy violation from the encoded feature alone.

active_recommendations.title: Rare-pattern investigation
active_recommendations.recommendation: Consider routing rare URL-feature patterns for additional inspection and analyst review instead of automatically blocking them solely because they are uncommon.
active_recommendations.priority_reason: Significant catalog of rare/unusual feature combinations identified for threat hunting triage.
active_recommendations.trigger_reason: Identified 138 distinct rare feature patterns encompassing 199 records (4.06% of dataset), exceeding minimum (5).
limitations: Do not automatically block or classify a record as malicious because its pattern is rare.
Describes infrequent combinations in historical phishing vectors.
